subject: Earth's oceans
title: What If Earth's Oceans Disappeared?

scenes.text: What if Earth's oceans disappeared overnight? Losing the beaches is the least of it.
First, 96.5 percent of Earth's water is gone. Only lakes, rivers, ice and groundwater are left.
Soon the rain starts failing. The oceans supply about 90 percent of the water that evaporates into the sky.
Then the heat has nowhere to go. The ocean has soaked up around 90 percent of global warming's extra heat.
And about half of Earth's oxygen comes from the ocean, made by tiny drifting plankton. That source vanishes too.
What's left is seven tenths of the planet as dry canyon, with one trench deep enough to swallow Everest whole.

description:
What if Earth's oceans disappeared? They hold 96.5% of the planet's water and supply about 90% of the water that evaporates into the water cycle.
They also absorb around 90% of the excess heat from global warming and produce about half of Earth's oxygen, and the deepest trench is about 7,000 feet deeper than Everest is tall.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: Which would you miss first: the rain, the beach or the air? Tell us the planet-sized what-if we should run through next.
